questions.question: 400 chickooes were bought at ₹1250 per hundred and were sold at a profit of ₹800. Find the selling price (in ₹) per dozen of chickooes.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost of 100 chickooes = ₹1250 ⇒ Cost Price (CP) of 400 chickooes = ₹5000

Total Selling Price (SP) of 400 chickooes = CP + Profit = 5000 + 800 = ₹5800

Selling Price of 1 dozen = (5800 ÷ 400) × 12 = 14.5 × 12 = ₹174

**∴ The correct answer is ₹174.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Quantity bought = 400 chickooes

Cost Price per hundred = ₹1250

Total Profit = ₹800

**Formula Used:**

Total Selling Price (SP) = Total Cost Price (CP) + Profit

Selling Price per dozen = (Total SP ÷ Total Quantity) × 12

 
 CP = ₹5000
 
 
 Profit = ₹800

 
 SP = CP + Profit = ₹5800
 
 Profit & Loss for 400 Chickooes
 
 SP per dozen = (5800 ÷ 400) × 12 = ₹174

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP for 400 chickooes = 4 × 1250 = ₹5000

⇒ Total SP for 400 chickooes = 5000 + 800 = ₹5800

⇒ Selling Price of 1 chickoo = 5800 ÷ 400 = ₹14.5

⇒ Selling Price of 1 dozen (12 chickooes) = 14.5 × 12 = ₹174

**∴ The correct answer is ₹174.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit & Loss Percentage

Profit or loss percentage is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP). Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always applied on the Marked Price (MP). The Selling Price is obtained as SP = MP − Discount.

Unitary Method

When items are priced in bulk, find the price of a single unit (Total Price ÷ Total Quantity) before calculating the price of the desired subset (like a dozen).

questions.question: If the price of petrol increases from ₹90/l to ₹110/l, by what percentage does a person have to decrease his consumption so that his expenditure on petrol remains the same (approximate to two decimals)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When expenditure is constant, consumption ratio is the inverse of the price ratio.

Price Ratio = 90 : 110 = 9 : 11 ⇒ Consumption Ratio = 11 : 9

Decrease in consumption = 11 − 9 = 2 units.

Percentage decrease = (2 ÷ 11) × 100 ≈ 18.18%

**∴ The correct answer is 18.18%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Original Price = ₹90/l

New Price = ₹110/l

**Formula Used:**

% Decrease = [ (New Price − Old Price) ÷ New Price ] × 100

 Expenditure Constant: Base Change Concept
 
• 
 
 
 ₹90
 ₹110
 Old Price
 New Price
 

 

 Price Increase = +₹20
 

 

 Consumption Decrease = -20 units
 New Base for % Calculation = 110

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let original consumption = C₁ and new consumption = C₂

⇒ Constant Expenditure = Price × Consumption

⇒ 90 × C₁ = 110 × C₂

⇒ C₂ / C₁ = 90 / 110 = 9 / 11

⇒ Consumption decrease = 11 − 9 = 2 units

⇒ % Decrease = (2 ÷ 11) × 100

⇒ % Decrease = 200 ÷ 11 = 18.1818...%

⇒ Approximate value = 18.18%

**∴ The correct answer is 18.18%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

Percentage change is calculated on the original base value: % Change = (Final − Initial) ÷ Initial × 100.

Product Constancy Rule

If A × B = Constant, then if A increases by a fraction x/y, B must decrease by x/(x+y) to keep the product unchanged.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the net percentage change is given by the formula: (a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100)%.

questions.question:
A shopkeeper offers 3 schemes of discounts to his customers. Which of the following schemes will fetch the minimum discount percentage?

A. Two successive discounts of 25% and 32%.

B. Buy 8 get two free.

C. Buy 8 and get 10.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective discount for Scheme A = 25 + 32 − (25 × 32) ÷ 100 = 57 − 8 = 49%.

Discount % for 'Buy X Get Y Free' = [Free Items ÷ Total Items] × 100.

Scheme B (Buy 8 get 2 free) = (2 ÷ 10) × 100 = 20%.

Scheme C (Buy 8 and get 10) means paying for 8 items and receiving 10 items, effectively getting 2 free.

So, Scheme C Discount = (2 ÷ 10) × 100 = 20%.

The minimum discount percentage is 20%, offered by both Scheme B and Scheme C.

**∴ The correct answer is Both B and C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Scheme A: Two successive discounts of 25% and 32%.

Scheme B: Buy 8 get 2 free.

Scheme C: Buy 8 and get 10.

**Formulas Used:**

Successive discount = x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100

Discount % = (Free articles ÷ Total articles) × 100%

 Scheme B & C : Buy 8, Get 2 Free
 
 Paid = 8 items
 Free = 2 items
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• 
 
 

 Total = 10 items
 
 Discount % = (2 ÷ 10) × 100 = 20%

**Calculations:**

⇒ **For Scheme A:**

⇒ Effective Discount = 25 + 32 − (25 × 32) ÷ 100

⇒ Effective Discount = 57 − 800 ÷ 100

⇒ Effective Discount = 57 − 8 = 49%

⇒ **For Scheme B:**

⇒ Free items = 2, Total items received = 8 + 2 = 10

⇒ Discount = (2 ÷ 10) × 100% = 20%

⇒ **For Scheme C:**

⇒ Paid for 8 items, but got a total of 10 items. So, free items = 10 − 8 = 2

⇒ Discount = (2 ÷ 10) × 100% = 20%

⇒ Comparing all the schemes (49%, 20%, 20%), the 20% minimum discount is given by Scheme B and Scheme C.

**∴ The correct answer is Both B and C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount

When two discounts of x% and y% are applied sequentially, the equivalent single discount percentage is given by [x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100]%.

Buy X Get Y Free

In these schemes, the discount percentage is strictly calculated based on the total items taken out of the shop. Discount % = [Y ÷ (X + Y)] × 100%.

Marked Price vs Cost Price

Discount is always evaluated on the overall Marked Price (MP). In 'Buy X Get Y Free' scenarios, the total Marked Price is the cumulative sum of all items in the basket, while the Selling Price (SP) matches the MP of only the items explicitly paid for.
</p

questions.question: Mohan invests a sum of ₹5400 and Varun invests a sum of ₹9400 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 6 years, Varun gets ₹480 more interest than Mohan, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in Principal = ₹9400 − ₹5400 = ₹4000

Difference in Simple Interest for 6 years = ₹480

Interest difference for 1 year = 480 ÷ 6 = ₹80

Rate of interest (R) = (80 ÷ 4000) × 100 = 2%

**∴ The correct answer is 2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 Mohan
 P = ₹5400
 Time = 6 yrs

 
 Varun
 P = ₹9400
 Time = 6 yrs

 

 
 SI Difference = ₹480

**Given:**

Mohan's investment (P₁) = ₹5400

Varun's investment (P₂) = ₹9400

Time (T) = 6 years

Let the rate of interest be R% per annum.

Difference in simple interest = ₹480

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI of Varun − SI of Mohan = 480

⇒ [(9400 × R × 6) ÷ 100] − [(5400 × R × 6) ÷ 100] = 480

⇒ [(9400 − 5400) × R × 6] ÷ 100 = 480

⇒ [4000 × R × 6] ÷ 100 = 480

⇒ 40 × 6 × R = 480

⇒ 240 × R = 480

⇒ R = 480 ÷ 240

⇒ R = 2%

**∴ The correct answer is 2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI) Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is Principal, R is Rate of Interest, and T is Time period.

Difference in Simple Interest

When the rate (R) and time (T) are the same, the difference in simple interest depends entirely on the difference in the principals: ΔSI = (ΔP × R × T) ÷ 100.

Amount Formula

Total Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI) = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought an article for ₹500. At what price (in ₹) should he sell the article to make 30% profit?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) is always considered as the base value of 100%.

To gain a 30% profit, the Selling Price (SP) must be 100% + 30% = 130% of CP.

SP = 130% of 500

SP = (130 ÷ 100) × 500 = 650

**∴ The correct answer is ₹650.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of the article = ₹500

Desired Profit = 30%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × [(100 + Profit%) ÷ 100]

 
 
 

 
 

 
 CP = ₹500
 100%

 

 
 
 + 30% Profit

 
 SP = ?
 130%

 SP = CP + Profit = 130% of CP

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 500 × [(100 + 30) ÷ 100]

⇒ SP = 500 × (130 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 5 × 130

⇒ SP = 650

**∴ The correct answer is ₹650.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

A profit is made when the Selling Price is greater than the Cost Price. The basic formula is Profit = SP − CP.

Profit Percentage

Profit % is calculated on the Cost Price as the base. Formula: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Discounts are always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Formula: Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount.

questions.question: The smallest natural number which is divisible by 11, 6, 55 and 9 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check the options using divisibility rules for the given numbers (11, 6, 55, 9).

For a number to be divisible by 55, it must end in 0 or 5. Options 921 and 1032 are instantly eliminated.

For a number to be divisible by 9, the sum of its digits must be a multiple of 9.

The sum of digits of 990 is 18 (divisible by 9), while for 1054 it is 10 (not divisible by 9).

Thus, 990 is the only option that satisfies all divisibility conditions.

**∴ The correct answer is 990.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 11, 6, 55, and 9.

**Formula Used:**

The smallest number completely divisible by a given set of numbers is their Least Common Multiple (LCM).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 11 = 11

⇒ Prime factorization of 6 = 2 × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 55 = 5 × 11

⇒ Prime factorization of 9 = 3 × 3 = 3²

⇒ LCM = Product of the highest powers of all involved prime factors

⇒ LCM = 2¹ × 3² × 5¹ × 11¹

⇒ LCM = 2 × 9 × 5 × 11

⇒ LCM = 10 × 99

⇒ LCM = 990

**∴ The correct answer is 990.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by each of the given numbers. It is found by taking the product of the highest powers of all prime factors present in the numbers.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The largest positive integer that divides each of the integers without leaving a remainder. It is found by taking the product of the lowest powers of only the common prime factors.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of its digits at odd places and the sum of its digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is perfectly divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits results in a value that is a multiple of 9.
</p

questions.question: A man goes to Jaipur from Surat at a speed of 3km/hr and returns to Surat at speed of 15km/hr, through same route. What is his average speed (in km/hr) of the entire journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When equal distances are covered at two different speeds x and y, the Average Speed = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Here, the going speed x = 3 km/hr and returning speed y = 15 km/hr.

Average Speed = (2 × 3 × 15) ÷ (3 + 15)

Average Speed = 90 ÷ 18 = 5 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from Surat to Jaipur (v₁) = 3 km/hr

Speed from Jaipur to Surat (v₂) = 15 km/hr

Let the one-way distance between Surat and Jaipur be D km.

 
 
 Surat

 
 Jaipur

 
 
• 
 Distance = D

 
 

 

 Speed = 3 km/hr

 
 

 

 Speed = 15 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = D (Surat to Jaipur) + D (Jaipur to Surat) = 2D

⇒ Time taken to reach Jaipur (t₁) = D ÷ 3

⇒ Time taken to return to Surat (t₂) = D ÷ 15

⇒ Total Time = (D ÷ 3) + (D ÷ 15)

⇒ Taking LCM of 3 and 15, Total Time = (5D + D) ÷ 15

⇒ Total Time = 6D ÷ 15 = 2D ÷ 5

⇒ Average Speed = 2D ÷ (2D ÷ 5)

⇒ Average Speed = (2D × 5) ÷ 2D = 5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Different Distances

When unequal distances d₁, d₂, d₃ are covered at variable speeds, the core formula remains: Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂ + d₃) ÷ (t₁ + t₂ + t₃).

Average Speed for 3 Equal Distances

If three equal distances are covered sequentially at speeds x, y and z, Average Speed = (3 × x × y × z) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Relative Speed

If two bodies move in the same direction, Relative Speed = |x − y|. If they move towards each other in opposite directions, Relative Speed = x + y.
</p

questions.question: What is the volume of a sphere of radius 3√2 cm?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The volume of a sphere can be calculated directly using the formula V = 4/3 × π × r³.

Substitute r = 3√2 cm into the formula.

Volume = 4/3 × π × (3√2)³

Volume = 4/3 × π × 54√2 = 72√2π cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 72√2π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the sphere (r) = 3√2 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a sphere = 4/3 × π × r³

 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
• 
 
 
 
 r = 3√2 cm

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = 4/3 × π × (3√2)³

⇒ Volume = 4/3 × π × (3³ × (√2)³)

⇒ Volume = 4/3 × π × (27 × 2√2)

⇒ Volume = 4/3 × π × 54√2

⇒ Volume = 4 × 18√2 × π

⇒ Volume = 72√2π cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 72√2π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Sphere

The total surface area of a sphere is given by the formula 4 × π × r², where r is the radius.

Volume of a Hemisphere

A hemisphere is half of a sphere. Its volume is given by 2/3 × π × r³.

Surface Area of a Hemisphere

The curved surface area of a hemisphere is 2 × π × r², and its total surface area is 3 × π × r².
</p

questions.question: P and Q can complete a piece of work in 28 days and 35 days, respectively. P begins to do the work and they work alternatively one at a time for one day each. In how many days will the whole work be completed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(28, 35) = 140 units.

Efficiency: P = 5, Q = 4. Combined work in 2 days (1 cycle) = 9 units.

15 full cycles (30 days) work = 15 × 9 = 135 units.

Remaining 5 units will be done by P on the 31st day in exactly 1 day.

Total time = 30 + 1 = 31 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 31 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P to complete the work = 28 days

Time taken by Q to complete the work = 35 days

P begins the work, and they work on alternate days.

**Concept Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Total Work = LCM of given days

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 P
 28
 140
 5
 
 

 Q
 35
 4
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done in 1st day by P = 5 units

⇒ Work done in 2nd day by Q = 4 units

⇒ Total work done in 2 days = 5 + 4 = 9 units

⇒ Number of such complete 2-day cycles possible for 140 units = 140 ÷ 9 = 15 cycles

⇒ Work done in 15 cycles (15 × 2 = 30 days) = 15 × 9 = 135 units

⇒ Remaining work = 140 − 135 = 5 units

⇒ On the 31st day, it is P's turn again. P can do 5 units of work per day.

⇒ Time taken by P to complete the remaining 5 units = 5 ÷ 5 = 1 day

⇒ Total time taken to complete the whole work = 30 + 1 = 31 days

**∴ The correct answer is 31 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Work Concept

When workers operate on alternate days, their combined work over the full cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 workers) is calculated first. Always evaluate the remainder carefully to check whose turn it is next to finish the remaining fractional work.

Pipes & Cisterns Analogy

Similar to alternate work, pipes functioning on alternate hours use the exact same LCM table format. If an outlet pipe is involved, its efficiency is strictly taken as negative while calculating the cycle capacity.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual total work done by each person. If workers work together for the exact same number of days, their wages can be directly distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.
</p

questions.question: The power consumption of an electrical device varies directly with the square of the voltage applied. If a device consumes 150 watts when the voltage is 120 volts, how much power (in watts) will it consume at 240 volts?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Power varies directly with the square of the voltage: P ∝ V²

Since the voltage is doubled (from 120 V to 240 V), the power consumed will be multiplied by 2² = 4.

New Power = 150 × 4 = 600 watts.

**∴ The correct answer is 600 watts.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Power (P₁) = 150 W

Initial Voltage (V₁) = 120 V

Final Voltage (V₂) = 240 V

**Formula Used:**

P ∝ V² ⇒ P₁ / V₁² = P₂ / V₂²

 
 Initial State
 V1 = 120 V
 P1 = 150 W
 
 

 

 Voltage × 2
 Power × 22
 
 
 Final State
 V2 = 240 V
 P2 = ?
 
 
 P2 = 150 × 4 = 600 W

**Calculations:**

⇒ 150 / 120² = P₂ / 240²

⇒ P₂ = 150 × (240 / 120)²

⇒ P₂ = 150 × (2)²

⇒ P₂ = 150 × 4

⇒ P₂ = 600

**∴ The correct answer is 600 watts.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Variation

When two quantities vary directly, an increase in one causes a proportional increase in the other. Formula: A = kB

Inverse Variation

When two quantities vary inversely, an increase in one causes a proportional decrease in the other. Formula: A = k / B

Joint Variation

When a quantity varies directly as the product of two or more other quantities. Formula: A = kBC
</p

questions.question: The speed of a stream is 6 km/h. A boat can go 56 km downstream and 39 km upstream in 7 hours. What is the speed (in km/h) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the given options to satisfy the time equation is the fastest method.

Total Time = Distance Downstream ÷ (u + 6) + Distance Upstream ÷ (u − 6) = 7

Checking Option 2 (15 km/h):

Time = 56 ÷ (15 + 6) + 39 ÷ (15 − 6) = 56 ÷ 21 + 39 ÷ 9

⇒ Time = 8/3 + 13/3 = 21/3 = 7 hours (Matches the given time).

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Total Time = 7 hours

**Given:**

Speed of stream (v) = 6 km/h

Total time taken (T) = 7 hours

Distance downstream = 56 km

Distance upstream = 39 km

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the boat in still water be u km/h.

Speed downstream = (u + 6) km/h

Speed upstream = (u − 6) km/h

⇒ 56 / (u + 6) + 39 / (u − 6) = 7

⇒ 56(u − 6) + 39(u + 6) = 7(u + 6)(u − 6)

⇒ 56u − 336 + 39u + 234 = 7(u² − 36)

⇒ 95u − 102 = 7u² − 252

⇒ 7u² − 95u − 150 = 0

Factorizing the quadratic equation:

⇒ 7u² − 105u + 10u − 150 = 0

⇒ 7u(u − 15) + 10(u − 15) = 0

⇒ (7u + 10)(u − 15) = 0

⇒ u = 15 or u = −10/7

Since speed cannot be negative, u = 15 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream Speed

When a boat travels in the direction of the stream, the effective speed is the sum of the boat's speed in still water and the stream's speed (u + v).

Upstream Speed

When a boat travels against the direction of the stream, the effective speed is the difference between the boat's speed in still water and the stream's speed (u − v).

Speed of Boat in Still Water

If downstream speed (D) and upstream speed (U) are given, then Speed of Boat = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream

If downstream speed (D) and upstream speed (U) are given, then Speed of Stream = (D − U) ÷ 2.

questions.question: If 3, 6, 12 and b are in continued proportion, then what is the value of **b**?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a continued proportion, consecutive terms are multiplied by a constant ratio.

Common ratio = Second term ÷ First term = 6 ÷ 3 = 2

Fourth term b = Third term × common ratio

⇒ b = 12 × 2 = 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Four numbers 3, 6, 12, and b are in continued proportion.

**Concept Used:**

For terms a, b, c, d in continued proportion, the ratio between consecutive terms is equal: a / b = b / c = c / d

 
 
 

 
 

 
 3

 

 × 2

 
 6

 

 × 2

 
 12

 

 × 2

 
 b = 24
 
 Continued Proportion Ratio = 2

**Calculation:**

⇒ 3 / 6 = 6 / 12 = 12 / b

⇒ 1 / 2 = 1 / 2 = 12 / b

Equating the last terms and cross-multiplying:

⇒ 1 / 2 = 12 / b

⇒ b = 12 × 2

⇒ b = 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Continued Proportion

When quantities are in continued proportion, the ratio between consecutive terms remains exactly the same. i.e., a / b = b / c = c / d.

Mean Proportional

For two numbers a and b, their mean proportional x satisfies a / x = x / b, which directly gives x = √(a × b).

Third Proportional

If a and b are two numbers, the third proportional c satisfies a / b = b / c, which can be solved as c = b² ÷ a.
</p

questions.question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹40 and compound interest is ₹56, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for Principal (P) when 2-year Simple Interest (SI) and Compound Interest (CI) are given:

P = (SI ÷ 2)² ÷ (CI − SI)

Substitute the given values (SI = 40, CI = 56):

P = (40 ÷ 2)² ÷ (56 − 40)

P = (20)² ÷ 16 = 400 ÷ 16 = 25

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time (T) = 2 years, SI = ₹40, CI = ₹56

**Formula Used:**

SI for 1 year = Total SI ÷ 2

CI for 2 years = Total SI + Interest on 1st year's SI

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 Principal (P)
 
 
 1st Yr SI = ₹20
 
 
 2nd Yr SI = ₹20
 
 
 CI - SI = ₹16
 
 Rate (R)
 Rate (R)
 Rate (R) on ₹20

 Total SI = 20 + 20 = ₹40 | Total CI = 20 + 20 + 16 = ₹56

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI for 1st year = 40 ÷ 2 = ₹20

⇒ Difference (CI − SI) = 56 − 40 = ₹16

⇒ This difference is simply the interest earned on the 1st year's SI.

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (16 ÷ 20) × 100 = 80%

⇒ We know that, SI for 1 year = (P × R × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ 20 = (P × 80) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (20 × 100) ÷ 80

⇒ P = 2000 ÷ 80 = ₹25

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference Between CI and SI for 2 Years

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years can be directly found using: D = P × (R ÷ 100)²

Difference Between CI and SI for 3 Years

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 3 years is given by: D = P × (R ÷ 100)² × (3 + R ÷ 100)

Ratio of CI and SI for 2 Years

For the same principal and rate of interest over 2 years, the ratio of CI to SI is expressed as: CI ÷ SI = 1 + (R ÷ 200)

questions.question: Nitin has ₹1224 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Pravin and Rishi and asked them to invest it at 4% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Pravin and Rishi got same amount after 14 and 15 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Nitin give to Rishi?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For equal amounts at Compound Interest, the ratio of shares P₁ / P₂ = (1 + R/100)t² − t¹.

Pravin's Share / Rishi's Share = (1 + 4/100)¹⁵ − ¹⁴ = 1.04 = 26/25.

Ratio of Pravin's share to Rishi's share = 26 : 25.

Rishi's Share = (25 / 51) × 1224 = ₹600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount Nitin has = ₹1224

Rate of interest (R) = 4% compounded annually

Time for Pravin (n₁) = 14 years

Time for Rishi (n₂) = 15 years

 
 Total = ₹1224
 
• 
 
• 
 
 Pravin
 Share = P
 Time = 14 years
 
 Rishi
 Share = R
 Time = 15 years
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 A1 = A2

**Formula Used:**

Amount in Compound Interest, A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let Pravin's share be P and Rishi's share be R.

⇒ Amount received by Pravin = P × (1 + 4/100)¹⁴

⇒ Amount received by Rishi = R × (1 + 4/100)¹⁵

⇒ Since both amounts are equal:

⇒ P × (1 + 4/100)¹⁴ = R × (1 + 4/100)¹⁵

⇒ P = R × (1 + 4/100)¹

⇒ P = R × (1 + 1/25)

⇒ P/R = 26/25

⇒ Total ratio units = 26 + 25 = 51 units

⇒ 51 units = ₹1224

⇒ 1 unit = 1224 ÷ 51 = 24

⇒ Rishi's share (R) = 25 units = 25 × 24 = 600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio of Principals for Equal Amounts

When a sum is divided into two parts invested at the same compound interest rate for different time periods such that their amounts are equal, the ratio of the principal amounts is inversely proportional to their respective multiplying factors raised to their time periods.

Compound Interest Multiplying Factor

The multiplying factor for compound interest is (1 + R/100). The amount after n years is the principal multiplied by this factor raised to the power n.

Rule of 72

A quick mental math shortcut to estimate the number of years required to double your money at a given annual rate of return: Years ≈ 72 ÷ Rate.

questions.question: The average weight of Kiran, Mahesh and Ram is 46 kg. If the average weight of Kiran and Mahesh be 40 kg and that of Mahesh and Ram be 47 kg, then the weight of Mahesh (in kg) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total sum of Kiran, Mahesh and Ram = 46 × 3 = 138 kg

Total sum of Kiran and Mahesh = 40 × 2 = 80 kg

Total sum of Mahesh and Ram = 47 × 2 = 94 kg

Weight of Mahesh = (Sum of first two) + (Sum of last two) − (Total Sum)

⇒ 80 + 94 − 138 = 174 − 138 = 36 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 36 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of Kiran, Mahesh and Ram = 46 kg

Average weight of Kiran and Mahesh = 40 kg

Average weight of Mahesh and Ram = 47 kg

**Formula Used:**

Total Value = Average × Number of Persons

 
 

 Total Weight (K + M + R) = 138 kg
 
 
 
 Kiran (K)

 
 Mahesh (M)

 
 Ram (R)

 
 

 K + M = 80 kg

 
 

 M + R = 94 kg

**Calculations:**

Let the weights of Kiran, Mahesh, and Ram be K, M, and R respectively.

⇒ Total weight of all three (K + M + R) = 46 × 3 = 138 kg

⇒ Total weight of Kiran and Mahesh (K + M) = 40 × 2 = 80 kg

⇒ Total weight of Mahesh and Ram (M + R) = 47 × 2 = 94 kg

Adding the sums of the two pairs:

⇒ (K + M) + (M + R) = 80 + 94

⇒ K + 2M + R = 174 kg

To find the weight of Mahesh (M), we subtract the total weight from this overlapping sum:

⇒ M = (K + 2M + R) − (K + M + R)

⇒ M = 174 − 138

⇒ M = 36 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 36 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Overlapping Averages

When averages of intersecting sub-groups are given, the common overlapping entity can easily be found by adding the totals of the sub-groups and subtracting the grand total of the entire group.

Inclusion of a New Member

If a new member joins a group and the overall average increases, the new member's value is greater than the previous average. The trick formula is: New Value = Old Average + (Change in Average × New Total Members).

Replacement Method

When an existing member is replaced by a new one, the difference in their values directly impacts the total sum. The shortcut formula is: Value of New Member = Value of Old Member + (Change in Average × Total Members).
</p

questions.question: A cyclist rides for 2 hours at 15 km/hr and then for 3 hours at 20 km/hr. What is the average speed (in km/hr) of the cyclist for the entire trip?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average speed is the weighted average of individual speeds using time as the weight.

Average Speed = (S₁ × T₁ + S₂ × T₂) ÷ (T₁ + T₂)

⇒ Average Speed = (15 × 2 + 20 × 3) ÷ (2 + 3)

⇒ Average Speed = (30 + 60) ÷ 5 = 90 ÷ 5 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed 1 (s₁) = 15 km/hr, Time 1 (t₁) = 2 hours

Speed 2 (s₂) = 20 km/hr, Time 2 (t₂) = 3 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 30 km
 
 

 60 km
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Total Distance = 90 km

 15 km/hr
 2 hours
 
 20 km/hr
 3 hours
 
 Average Speed = 90 ÷ 5 = 18 km/hr

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered in first part = 15 × 2 = 30 km

⇒ Distance covered in second part = 20 × 3 = 60 km

⇒ Total Distance = 30 + 60 = 90 km

⇒ Total Time = 2 + 3 = 5 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 90 ÷ 5 = 18 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (General Formula)

It is the ratio of total distance travelled to the total time taken for the entire journey. Formula: Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When a person covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is directly given by the formula 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = |x − y|. When they are moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = x + y.
</p
